title: TATG: Tracking-Aware Testing Objective for LLM-based Test Generation
datasets: 110 focal methods from the KTester benchmark, drawn from 10 open-source projects and fixed project versions.

31 purposively selected additional focal methods from 10 projects related to MocklessTester, including Defects4J projects and modern Java repositories. The paper identifies nine methods drawn from fixed Defects4J project revisions; it does not evaluate Defects4J bug IDs or buggy/fixed pairs. This is method-level test-generation, not historical bug reproduction.
task: Java/JUnit focal-method test generation with static/semantic test objectives, iterative compilation/execution and coverage feedback, followed by mutation-guided assertion hardening.
input_setting: Current/fixed project source and focal methods; generated tests are evaluated against the same code. No bug report, historical buggy/fixed checkout pair, or root-cause label is the task input.
author_artifact_url: No TATG implementation URL in paper. Author-linked profile checked: https://github.com/Amocy-Wang; paper says implementation and benchmark subjects “will be made publicly available.”
author_relationship_evidence: The paper does not provide a code/data URL or repository identifier and describes release as future work. Checked arXiv full text, exact-title/public-code web search, and first author Guancheng Wang’s public GitHub profile/repository listing; no TATG repository or package was found. GitHub profile identity matches first author name and Lero affiliation, but the profile is not itself a TATG artifact.
source_commit_or_archive: No author implementation, benchmark subject manifest, or immutable source snapshot located as of 2026-10-15. Referenced projects (KTester, MocklessTester, SootUp, etc.) are inputs/dependencies, not the TATG implementation.
license: Paper is licensed CC BY 4.0 per arXiv. No software or benchmark-data license can be verified because the promised TATG artifact was not located.
exact_models: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B locally served using vLLM, default configuration, temperature 0.2.
DeepSeek-V4-Flash-284B served via Fireworks AI with the same generation configuration.
Industrial comparison on 50 focal methods uses GLM-5.2-753B; this is a proprietary tool/model setting, not the main open-model experiment.
Traditional/mixed baselines: EvoSuite, Randoop, EvoObj, KTester, PANTA, and MUTGEN; evaluation uses JaCoCo and PITest default mutators.
weights_status: No TATG fine-tuned weights reported. The paper names two released models, but does not provide immutable model revisions/hashes in the paper text. DeepSeek route is hosted; reproducing exact served snapshot/config is not verified.
evaluation_route: Read all 9,403 extracted words of arXiv v1 (main sections, conclusion and references); confirmed abstract/main-text claims against arXiv entry. Evaluation covers 141 methods (110 KTester + 31 additional), 900-second per-focal traditional-generation budget, up to 1,800 seconds for TATG, 5 structural + 5 hardening rounds, Bmin=1/Bmax=50/λ=1, fixed seed 3 for EvoSuite/Randoop/EvoObj, JaCoCo/PITest. The paper reports Qwen3.6 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash results and promises public implementation/subjects, but no usable package was found. No code executed and no model/API call made.
blockers: The author implementation and benchmark subject manifest are promised but no public TATG artifact or stable snapshot was found.

Without source, the static objective extraction, feedback-state transitions, project-specific build setup, test harness and 141-method manifest cannot be reconstructed for exact reproduction; we did not reimplement them.

The experimental subjects are fixed-code focal methods rather than historical buggy/fixed Defects4J or BugsInPy cases, so the reported coverage/mutation results do not validate real issue reproduction or root-cause localization.
The paper does not pin exact immutable model revisions; one model is a hosted Fireworks route and the 50-method industrial comparison uses proprietary GLM-5.2-753B.
concept_fit: Very high as direct prior work for explicit behavioral test obligations: cards encode source evidence, prerequisite setup, target action, oracle shape, measurable acceptance predicate, lifecycle status and behavioral de-duplication key. This overlaps substantially with concept-guided testing and weak-oracle hardening; novelty must be distinguished by source-grounded concept semantics, bug-revealing intent, and historical bug-reproduction evaluation.
recommendation: Keep as a close prior-work/novelty comparator, not a currently reproducible base. Its methodology is highly relevant to our concept-guided test generation, especially obligation tracking and separating reachability from oracle strength. Do not describe its fixed-method coverage/mutation evaluation as Defects4J bug reproduction; revisit only if authors release the promised implementation and task manifest. A future own-model evaluation may be feasible after that release, without rerunning the proprietary industrial comparison.
